events.title: Battle of Cajamarca
events.description: Spanish conquistador Francisco Pizarro and a small force ambushed and captured Inca emperor Atahualpa in Cajamarca, Peru, killing thousands of his unarmed attendants and soldiers.
events.significance: The capture of Atahualpa was a decisive step in the Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire, which led to the collapse of the largest pre-Columbian empire in the Americas and the establishment of Spanish colonial rule in South America.

events.title: Oklahoma Admitted as the 46th U.S. State
events.description: President Theodore Roosevelt issued a proclamation admitting Oklahoma to the Union, merging Oklahoma Territory and Indian Territory into a single state.
events.significance: Statehood ended the separate Indian Territory, where several Native American nations had been relocated, and reshaped the political and cultural landscape of the American Southwest and Plains.

events.title: United States Recognizes the Soviet Union
events.description: President Franklin D. Roosevelt established formal diplomatic relations with the Soviet Union after sixteen years of nonrecognition following the 1917 Bolshevik Revolution, following an agreement with Foreign Minister Maxim Litvinov.
events.significance: The recognition opened official channels between the two powers, laying groundwork for their later wartime alliance during World War II and shaping the dynamics of 20th-century geopolitics.

events.title: UNESCO Founded
events.description: The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization was established when its constitution was signed in London by representatives of 37 countries.
events.significance: UNESCO became the UN agency for promoting international cooperation in education, science, and culture, and it designates World Heritage Sites to protect cultural and natural landmarks worldwide.

events.title: Death of Pioneering Computer Scientist Not Applicable: Launch of Mars Global Surveyor Preceded
events.description: On November 7, 1996, Mars Global Surveyor launched; on November 16, 1974, the Arecibo message was transmitted to the globular star cluster M13 to demonstrate human technological capability.
events.significance: The Arecibo message remains one of humanity's most famous deliberate attempts to send a signal into space and sparked ongoing debate on communication with extraterrestrial intelligence.
